Condition : 1 - Time limits
The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
Condition : 2 - Time limit (Outline Permission)
The first application for the approval of Reserved Matters for the development hereby approved shall be made to the local planning authority before the expiration of four years from the date of this permission. All other applications for Reserved Matters shall be submitted before the expiration of four years from the date of approval of the previous Reserved Matters application. The final application for the approval of reserved matters for the final Phase of the development shall be submitted to the local planning authority no later than eight years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
Condition : 3 - Programme of Phasing
Any reserved matters application shall be accompanied by a programme specifying when the following will be delivered relative to the development to which the reserved matters application relates:

�	Hard/soft landscaping;

�	Other public realm.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved programme. 

Reason: To ensure satisfactory comprehensive development and proper planning of the area.
Condition : 4 - Time limits for Reserved Matters
Any Phase of development hereby permitted shall be commenced before the expiration of three years from the date of any approval of Reserved Matters relating to that Phase, or in the event of grant of more than one Reserved Matters approval on different dates, within 3 years of approval of the last Reserved Matter.
Reason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).
Condition : 5 - Accordance with approved plans

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the details contained in the Design Code Rev P02 dated 12 January 2026. Each application for Reserved Matters shall demonstrate compatibility with the Design Code.
Reason: To ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the Development Plan and to ensure the delivery of high quality design as approved planning permission.

Condition : 11 - Submission of Reserved Matters
In respect of any proposals other than those forming the Detailed Element of the development as identified on plan, details of the following matters, GWR-HTL-ZZ-ZZ-DR-A-P0001 Rev P01 (reserved matters) as relevant to that Phase shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and no work except for demolition, site clearance and remediation shall start within the relevant Phase (or part therein) until the Local Planning Authority has approved all of the reserved matters for that Phase:
�	Layout (to include details of the areas to be used for each land use, including car and cycle parking)
�	Appearance

Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interest of proper planning, and to comply with the EIA Directive and to ensure that high standards of urban design, landscaping and environmental mitigation are achieved, and a proper record is kept, and in order that the Council may be satisfied as to the details of the development in the interests of the visual amenity of the area and to satisfy the requirements of Local and Local Plan Polices.
Condition : 12 - Wayfinding and Signage Strategy
No part of the relevant Phase shall be occupied until details of a Wayfinding and Signage Strategy, for each Phase, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The Wayfinding and Signage Strategy shall refer to Transport for London's Legible London initiatives and include the surrounding streets to inform existing residents and visitors to the area of these new routes to the facilities in the development. 
The approved Wayfinding and Signage Strategy for each Phase shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details and made available for use before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use for the relevant Phase (or part therein) and retained thereafter.
Reason: To emphasize the traffic-free routes through the site and to support sustainable transport objectives in accordance with adopted policies
Condition : 13 - Wind Mitigation
prior to any above ground works in each Phase, details of Wind Mitigation as outlined within Environmental Statement, Volume 1, Chapter 10, Wind and Microclimate 2025 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved mitigation measures shall be implemented at all stages of the development in full and retained and maintained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: To ensure an acceptable functional quality of the buildings and spaces in accordance with
Condition : 14 - Shopfronts and Signage Details 
No occupation of any commercial unit within the detailed plots (M, K, G, I, L, B1, B2, F, H) shall take place until full details of all shopfronts have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA).
The submission shall include:
�	Scaled drawings (minimum 1:20) of each shopfront elevation and section, showing:
�	Stall risers, pilasters, framing, and glazing proportions.
�	Door and window details, including materials, colours, and finishes.
�	Benchmark palette for core elements � fascia, projecting, shutters, hanging, frontages, as well as details for individual components.

Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained thereafter.

An advertisement consent shall be obtained in any case where an advertisement is required.

The Reserved Matters applications shall accord with the approved Design Code.

Commercial units within the outline component shall not be occupied until details of the individual shopfronts have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved Design Code.

Reason: To ensure high-quality, coordinated shopfront and signage design that enhances the character and appearance of the development and avoids visual clutter.
Condition : 15 - Sound Insulation 
A.	Prior to the commencement of each Phase of development above ground level (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works), details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority showing sound insulation measures, including anticipated noise levels within the dwellings hereby permitted as a result of those measures, for the floor/ceiling/wall structures separating the commercial part of the development from those dwellings.
Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
B.	For each Phase, none of the relevant residential accommodation shall be occupied until the measures installed have been tested and proven to be effective in accordance with a scheme that has previously been
submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved measures shall be permanently retained thereafter.

Reason: To provide acceptable living conditions for future residents in accordance with Local Plan and London Plan.
Condition : 16 - Internal Water Use
For each Phase, prior to the first occupation of any residential development, evidence (schedule of installed fittings and manufactures literature) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development has achieved an internal water use of 105L/person/day or less.
Reason: in order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources in accordance with London Borough of Hounslow Local Plan Policy EQ2.
Condition : 17 - External Lighting Strategy (Detailed Blocks M, K, G, I, L, B1, B2, F, H)
No above ground works (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works) within the Detailed Element shall commence until a comprehensive External Lighting Strategy should be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA) and implemented.
The strategy shall include:
i.	Layout plan showing the location of all external lighting, including:

�	Bollards, columns, and under croft/flyover lighting.
�	Feature and landscape lighting, particularly at junctions with Boston Manor Park (cycle route to Block A, main Boulevard to BMP and under flyover connection) and public routes.

�	Luminaire design, materials, and finishes.

iii.	Lighting controls:

iv.	Environmental and safety impact assessment:

v.	Ecology considerations, including avoidance of upward light spill near green corridors, Boston Manor Park, and the River Brent to protect wildlife.

vi.	Compliance statement confirming alignment with:

Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved strategy and maintained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a safe, sustainable, and visually appropriate l
Condition : 18 - Play Equipment
Prior to the commencement of above ground works (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works) within any Development Plot in which play space is to be located, detailed specifications of all play equipment to be provided within each relevant area of public open space shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
A)	Quantum of playspace
B)	How the quantum contributes to play space for each plot and the masterplan as a whole
C)	Surface treatment, sitting, design, equipment and features
D)	Consideration of play accessibility
E)	Site management controls
The approved play equipment shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to any residential occupation in the relevant development plot.
Reason: To ensure high quality play spaces
Condition : 19 - Housing Standards Residential
For each Reserved Matters application submitted to the Local Planning Authority, details shall be provided to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that all
residential (Use Class C3) floorspace meets the Minimum Internal Space Standards for new homes, as set out in Table 3.1 of London Plan (2021) Policy D6, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to ensure all residential units achieve an appropriate standard of accommodation in accordance with Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021).
Condition : 20 - Fire Statement
For each Reserved Matters application submitted to the Local Planning Authority, a Fire Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Each Fire Statement shall accord with the measures set out within the approved site-wide Fire Strategy, and those measures shall be implemented within each Phase of development. All Fire Statements shall be subject to consultation with the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) under Planning Gateway One, where required.
Reason: To ensure the highest standards of fire safety are secured and implemented across the site, in accordance with Policy CD16 of the Local Plan 2024 and Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021).
Condition : 21 - PD restriction (commercial)
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Approved Development) Order (England) 2015, as amended (or any order revoking and reenacting that order with or without modification), any non-residential development hereby approved shall be used only for purposes falling within the Use Class associated with the first established use of the premises, and for no other use as defined within this use class or its associated approved change of use in the Order.
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order), no change of use under Part 3 Class M or Class O, Class PA, enlargement of the premises or any additional structures/buildings within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out.
Shall the proposed use precede a full planning application is required.
Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining properties, but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Use Class to protect nearby land uses and the character of the area.
Condition : 22 - PD restriction general other
No cables, wires, aerials, pipework (except any rainwater downpipes as shown on the approved drawings), meter boxes or flues shall be fixed to any elevation facing a highway unless prior written approval is gained from the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: To protect the appearance of the area and the
neighbours' living conditions.
Condition : 23 - Restriction on Alternative Uses (Plots J1 and J2)

The floorspace within Plots J1 and J2 shall be used only for purposes falling within Use Class E(g) and/or Class F1(a), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Any proposal for an alternative use shall be supported by evidence demonstrating that the delivery or occupation of Use Class E(g) and/or Class F1(a) floorspace is not viable, including a minimum of two years of continuous marketing at market rates and an independent viability assessment, all to be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Where such evidence is approved, only Use Class B2 and/or B8 uses may be permitted, and only to the extent approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To secure the delivery and retention of employment and educational floorspace and to ensure that any alternative use is justified by robust viability and marketing evidence.
Condition : 24 - Land quality - intrusive site investigation
For Each Phase, prior to any above-ground construction within the Detailed Element (excluding enabling works), a Phase 2 Intrusive Site Investigation Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA.
The report shall identify contamination extent, update the CSM, and propose remediation measures where necessary, in accordance with UK guidance and best practice.
Reason: To ensure contamination risks are properly assessed before construction.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work.
(ii)	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the local planning authority may stipulate if this report is found to be insufficient or where it is deemed necessary to secure adequate safety for future site users.
(iv)	Suitable testing shall be undertaken in accordance with the potential contaminants identified in the Conceptual Site Model (CSM), and any unexpected/suspected contaminants encountered during the investigations.
(v)	Documentation of building demolition - for instance asbestos removal - should contribute to the Phase II report.
(vi)	The Council requests that site investigation reports or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 25 - Land quality � Remediation Method Statement/ Remediation Strategy
For each Phase, where remediation is required, following the results of the Intrusive Site Investigation, prior to any above- ground construction within the Detailed Element (excluding enabling works), a Remediation Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA.
The statement shall detail and include verification requirements. Reason: To ensure remediation before occupation.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority.
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 26 - Land quality � additional/unexpected
If unexpected contamination found during development During the development:
Hybrid Trigger (applies to both Detailed and Outline Elements): If unexpected contamination is found during any development Phase, works in the affected area shall cease immediately. The LPA shall be notified, and within one month of discovery, a Revised Remediation Method Statement shall be submitted for approval.
Further works shall not resume until the revised statement is approved and implemented.
Reason: To ensure unforeseen contamination is managed safely.
Supporting notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(ii)	In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 27 - Land quality - verification and validation of remedial work
For each Phase, Prior to the first occupation of any building or plot within the Detailed Element, the agreed remediation scheme (including any approved amendments) for that area shall be fully implemented. A Verification Report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA).
The report must revisit the Conceptual Site Model, confirm all remediation steps were completed in accordance with UK guidance and best practice, and address any unexpected contamination encountered during development.
Reason: To ensure the development is safe for occupation and meets environmental standards across all Phases.
Supporting notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement.
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 28 - Land quality - long term monitoring and maintenance
Where long-term monitoring or maintenance is required following completion of remedial measures for any building/plot within the Detailed Element, a Monitoring & Maintenance Plan shall be submitted to the relevant Phase and approved in writing by the LPA prior to first occupation of that building/plot. Reports demonstrating effectiveness shall then be submitted in accordance with the approved timescale.
All monitoring and maintenance shall follow current UK guidance and best practice.
Reason: To ensure ongoing protection of human health, controlled waters, and ecological systems throughout the life of the development.
Condition : 29 - Landscaping and Public Realm
No development above ground level (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works) shall commence until a detailed scheme of hard and soft landscaping of the details shown on approved plans has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall:
(a)	Set out the design objectives and demonstrate how the proposals deliver the approved character areas
(b)	Provide existing and proposed levels or contours, including treatment of level changes to ensure accessibility, sections in a minimum of 1:20 scale.
(c)	Include details of boundary treatments, retaining structures, and edge conditions to soften transitions and restore ecological links.
(d)	Show vehicle parking layouts and pedestrian priority routes, including step-free access and safe crossings.
(e)	Specify hard surfacing materials, ensuring SuDS compliance and climate resilience.
(f)	Identify minor artefacts and structures (e.g., seating, play equipment, lighting, signage, refuse storage, CCTVs, and public art installations).
(g)	Detail functional services above and below ground, including drainage, utilities, power, communications cables, pipelines, etc. and irrigation systems for green roofs and planted areas.
Confirm retained historic or landscape features and proposals for restoration where relevant.
(i)	Include planting plans and specifications, covering: Cultivation and establishment operations.
Plant schedules with species, sizes, and densities prioritising native and pollinator-friendly species.

Biodiversity enhancements and habitat creation
(j)	Provide details of renewable energy installations within the landscape (where applicable).

(h)	Reason: To secure a high-quality, inclusive, and ecologically responsive landscape that reflects the site's design vision, promotes biodiversity, and ensures climate resilience.
Condition : 30 - Boundary Treatment
Prior to above-ground works commencing (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works) within the Detailed Element, a plan indicating the positions, design, materials, and type of additional boundary or hoarding treatment to be erected around the perimeter of the Detailed Element and along any interface with undeveloped Outline land shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA).
The approved boundary treatment shall:
�	Provide security and visual screening during construction.
�	Avoid prejudice to future Outline development.
The boundary treatment shall be erected as approved prior to first occupation of any building within the Detailed Element and retained until permanent landscaping or development in adjoining Outline areas is completed.
The approved boundary treatment shall be erected as approved prior to first occupation of any part of that Phase/Plot and retained thereafter.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions, ensure site security and visual amenity during Phased development, and maintain a satisfactory appearance of the site and surrounding area.
Condition : 31 - Tree survey & protection
For each Phase, prior to development (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works), the following details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA):
A plan showing the position of each tree within the Detailed Element and on land adjacent to the site (including street trees and trees outside the red line boundary) that could influence or be affected by the development, indicating which trees are to be removed.
A schedule for each identified tree listing species, diameter, approximate height, and an assessment of general health and stability, as a minimum requirement of BS 5837- 2012 (or any subsequent British Standard), including any proposed pruning, felling, or other works.
Details of any proposed alterations to existing ground levels and the position of any proposed excavation that may affect the root protection area of retained trees.
Details of fencing and other protective measures to be installed for the protection of retained trees.
The approved tree protection measures shall be implemented at the commencement of works and retained for the duration of development within the Detailed Element.

Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and surrounding area, protect trees both within and adjacent to the site (including those outside the red line boundary), and promote biodiversity.
Condition : 32 - Tree planting
For each Phase, prior to development (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works) shall commence until a full specification of all proposed tree planting has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA).
The specification shall include:
Quantity, size, species, and positions or density of all trees to be planted within the Detailed Element and on land adjacent to the site (including street trees and trees outside the red line boundary where planting is proposed).
Planting methods, protection measures, and proposed times of planting.
Implementation and Maintenance (applies to both Parts):
(b) b) All trees shall be planted in accordance with the approved specification and prior to occupations and within the dormant
growth period in compliance with British Standard 8545:2014 (or any subsequent British Standard).
(c) Any tree that, within five years of planting, dies, is cut down, uprooted, destroyed, or becomes seriously damaged or diseased (in the opinion of the LPA) shall be replaced with another tree of similar size and species during the next planting season.
Reason: To ensure a high-quality landscape design, protect and enhance biodiversity, and maintain a satisfactory appearance of the site and surrounding area, including land outside the red line boundary where relevant.
Condition : 33 - Green Roofs
For each Phase prior to their installation, full details of the proposed green roofs shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (LPA). The details shall include:
�	Construction drawings (plan and cross-sections); Planting schedule using a native wildflower seed mix (turf or sedum blanket will not be accepted);
�	Substrate depth between 80mm�150mm, undulating and containing varied materials (sand, gravel, crushed ceramic, brick, recycled inert materials);
�	Provision of small piles of untreated logs for habitat creation;
�	No irrigation;
�	Confirmation that green roof construction will be supervised by a suitably qualified landscape/ecology contractor.
�	The approved details shall be implemented and retained permanently thereafter.
The approved details shall be implemented and retained permanently thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a high-quality, biodiverse green roof design that enhances the appearance of the development and promotes ecological value.
Condition : 34 - Ecological Management Plan
For each Phase, no development shall take place (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works) until an Ecological Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
The Ecological Management Plan shall incorporate:
�	details of measures to protect breeding birds, nests and eggs from mortality/damage, injury and disturbance, including avoidance by timing and/or appropriate supervision;
�	details of the ecological clerk of works supervision to be put in place to monitor the clearance of vegetation to minimise impact on undiscovered or other unexpected faunal encounters;
�	an ecological lighting plan;
�	details of ecological enhancement and urban greening factor, including how the urban greening factor is to be delivered and achieved on site;
�	details of how the enhancement measures will be monitored, managed and maintained, including the long- term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules;
�	additional detail on location and type of bird/bat boxes, maintenance and a commitment that any data collected is to be shared with the Council;
�	species surveys within and around the site to demonstrate ecological enhancements
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In the interests of nature conservation.

Condition : 35 - Urban Greening Factor
The development shall be designed and delivered to achieve a minimum Urban Greening Factor (UGF) score of 0.4, in accordance with the submitted document. Details demonstrating compliance with the required UGF shall be submitted with each Reserved Matters application and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure the delivery of high-quality urban greening across the development, in accordance with Policy GB14 of the Local Plan 2024, the Greening SPD, and Policy G5 of the London Plan (2021).
Condition : 36 - Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG)
The proposed development shall deliver a minimum Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) of 10% for area habitats and slightly 0% for watercourse habitats. Each Reserved Matters application shall include details demonstrating how the proposed landscaping, habitat creation, and ecological measures contribute to achieving the overall site-wide Biodiversity Net Gain targets, and these details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure the development delivers measurable biodiversity enhancements.

Condition : 37 - Construction Environment Management Plan
No development on each Phase shall take place (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works), until a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP), for each Phase, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The CEMP shall provide as a minimum:
�	confirmation that a pre-start records of site conditions on the adjoining
�	public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a
�	commitment to repair any damage caused.
�	The approved Plan shall be adhered to throughout the construction period.
Reason: In order to ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat, and secure opportunities for the enhancement of the nature conservation value of the site and safeguard the environment and in the interests of the structural integrity of the waterway and to ensure the proposed works do not have any adverse impact on the safety of waterway users and the integrity of the Grand Union canal

Email:developer.services@thameswater.co.uk Phone: 0800 009 3921 (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm) Write to: Thames Water Developer Services, Clearwater Court, Vastern Road, Reading, Berkshire RG1 8DB
Condition : 74 - Thames Water - Sufficient Capacity
Each Phase shall not be occupied until confirmation has been provided that either:
-	all water network upgrades required to accommodate the additional demand to serve the development have been completed; or
-	A development and infrastructure Phasing plan has been agreed with Thames Water to allow development to be occupied. Where a development and infrastructure Phasing plan is agreed, no occupation shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed development and infrastructure Phasing plan.
Reason - The development may lead to no / low water pressure, and network reinforcement works are anticipated to be necessary to ensure that sufficient capacity is made available to accommodate additional demand anticipated from the new development. The developer can request information to support the discharge of this condition by visiting the Thames Water website at thameswater.co.uk/preplanning. Should the Local Planning Authority consider the above recommendation inappropriate or be unable to include it in the decision notice, it is important that the Local Planning Authority liaises with Thames Water Development Planning Department (email: devcon.team@thameswater.co.uk) prior to the planning application approval.
Condition : 75 - Thames Water - Build Over Agreement
No development shall take place within 3 metres of a public sewer and/or within 1 metre of a public lateral drain unless and until details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with Thames Water, demonstrating that appropriate arrangements have been made to prevent damage to the sewer network and ensure suitable and safe access for maintenance and repairs. Any approved works shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: Public sewers are crossing or close to the development. This is to prevent damage to the sewer network and ensure suitable and safe access to carry out maintenance and repairs.
Condition : 76 - Air Quality
For each Phase no development (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works) shall commence until a Construction Air Quality Management Plan (CAQMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CAQMP shall include measures for dust control, Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) compliance, and monitoring arrangements. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details."
Reason: In the interests of air quality and to protect neighbours'
living conditions and the wider local environment.
Condition : 77 - For each Phase, prior to the commencement of development (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works), evidence should be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that the
development has made sufficient provisions to enable the connection to a feasible district heating network in the future, including a safeguarded pipe route for future connections at the site boundary.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 78 - Archaeology
Prior to the commencement of each Phase of development, a written scheme of investigation (WSI) should be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, which shall include the statement of significance and research objectives, and
A.	The programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works
B.	Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits
C.	The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the WSI
Reasons: In order to safeguard the architectural and historic interest.
Condition : 79 - Unexpected Archaeology
In the event of the discovery of archaeological remains which cannot be examined within the scope of a watching brief, then development will cease until a detailed scheme of excavation and recording has been agreed with GLAAS.
Should any archaeological remains be discovered in the course of development, it is recommended that the developer contact glaas@HistoricEngland.org.uk so that an assessment can be made for the formulation of mitigating measures or the instigation of contingency procedures. If human remains are found, work should cease immediately
Reasons: In order to safeguard the architectural and historic interest.
Condition : 80 - Standard Aviation Conditions
1.	For each Phase, No construction shall commence on site (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works), unless there has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and by the Radar Operator - NATS (En-route) plc, either detailed plans or evidence for the proposed buildings in that individual Phase, demonstrating that there would be no detrimental impact upon the operation of the H10 SSR Radar, OR, details of a 'Radar Mitigation Scheme' (including a timetable for its implementation during construction) to mitigate any detrimental impact upon the H10 SSR Radar.
2.	Where a 'Radar Mitigation Scheme' has been required, no construction above 25m above ground level shall take place on site, unless the 'Radar Mitigation Scheme' has been implemented. Development shall not take place other than in complete accordance with such a scheme as so approved unless the planning authority and NATS (En-route) plc have given written consent for a variation.
Reason: In the interests of Air Traffic Safety and of the operations of NATS En-route PLC.
Condition : 81 - Bird Hazard Management Plan
For each Phase, development shall not commence (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works) until a Bird Hazard Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted plan shall include details of:
- Management of any flat/shallow pitched/green roofs on buildings within the site which may be attractive to nesting, roosting and "loafing" birds. The Bird Hazard Management Plan shall be implemented as approved and shall remain in force for the life of the buildings. No subsequent alterations to the plan are to take place unless first submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: It is necessary to manage the flat roofs to minimise its attractiveness to birds which could endanger the safe movement of aircraft and the operation of Heathrow Airport.
Information The Bird Hazard Management Plan must ensure that flat/shallow pitched roofs be constructed to allow access to all areas by foot using permanent fixed access stairs ladders or similar. The owner/occupier must not allow gulls, to nest, roost or
loaf on the building. Checks must be made weekly or sooner if bird activity dictates, during the breeding season. Outside of the breeding season gull activity must be monitored and the roof checked regularly to ensure that gulls do not utilise the roof. Any gulls found nesting, roosting or loafing must be dispersed by the owner/occupier when detected or when requested by Heathrow Airside Operations staff. In some instances, it may be necessary to contact Heathrow Airside Operations staff before bird dispersal takes place. The owner/occupier must remove any nests or eggs found on the roof. The breeding season for gulls typically runs from March to June. The owner/occupier must obtain the appropriate licences where applicable from Natural England before the removal of nests and eggs.
Condition : 82 - Construction Management Strategy
For each Phase, Development shall not commence until a construction management strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority covering the application site and any adjoining land which will be used during the construction period. Such a strategy shall include the following matters: details of cranes and other tall construction equipment (including the details of obstacle lighting) � Such schemes shall comply with Advice Note 4 'Cranes' (available at http://www.aoa.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/Advice-Note- 4-Cranes-2016.pdf).  The approved strategy (or any variation approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority) shall be implemented for the duration of the construction period.
Reason: To ensure that construction work and construction equipment on the site and adjoining land does not breach the Instrument Flight Procedural surfaces associated to Heathrow Airport and endanger aircraft movements and the safe operation of the aerodrome.
Condition : 83 - Permanent Obstacle Lighting Scheme
Obstacle lights shall be placed on the top corners of the proposed building (Block H), and subject to the height of the surrounding buildings, further intermediate obstacle lights might be required to be installed down the sides of each corner. These obstacle lights must be steady state red lights with a minimum intensity of 2000 candelas. Periods of illumination of obstacle lights, obstacle light locations and obstacle light photometric performance must all be in accordance with the requirements of UK Regulation (EU) 139-2014.
Reason: Permanent illuminated obstacle lights are required on the development to avoid endangering the safe movement of aircraft and the operation of Heathrow Airport.
Condition : 84 - Timing of vegetation clearance (breeding birds)
All removal of trees, hedgerows, shrubs, scrub or tall herbaceous vegetation shall be undertaken between September and February inclusive. If this is not possible, then a suitably qualified ecologist shall check the areas concerned immediately prior to the clearance works to ensure that no nesting or nest-building birds are present.
If any nesting birds are present, then the vegetation shall not be removed until the fledglings have left the nest.
Reason: All wild birds, their nests and young are protected during the nesting period under The Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended). In the interests of nature conservation and biodiversity, in accordance with Local Plan Policy GB7.
Condition : 85 - Health Impact Assessment
For each Phase, no above-ground works shall take place until a proportionate Health Impact Assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Planning Authority. The HIA shall:
a)	identify likely significant health effects arising from the development,
b)	set	out	mitigation/enhancement	measures	(including design-led interventions) and delivery responsibilities, and
c)	include an implementation plan.
The development shall proceed in accordance with the approved HIA, and the agreed measures shall be completed prior to first occupation of the relevant Phase or as otherwise agreed in writing.
Reason: To secure a healthy, safe and inclusive environment and to ensure that health considerations are integrated into the design and delivery of the development.
Condition : 86 - Odour Monitoring � External Sources

No development hereby permitted shall be occupied until an Odour Management Review (OMR) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The OMR shall assess the potential for odour impacts arising from off-site
industrial and waste-management activities, including but not limited to facilities along Transport Avenue, and shall identify any proportionate mitigation required to ensure that future occupants are not exposed to unacceptable levels of odour nuisance.

Where mitigation is identified as necessary, a scheme detailing the design, implementation, and maintenance of such measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to first occupation. The development shall thereafter be carried out and operated in full accordance with the approved details. 
 
This requirement shall apply to all relevant submissions pursuant to both full and outline applications.

Reason: To ensure that future residents are protected from potential odour arising from industrial and waste-management uses.
Condition : 87 - River Brent Landscape and Ecological Management Plan
For each Phase, no development (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works) shall take place until a landscape and ecological management plan, including long-term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for all landscaped areas (except privately owned domestic gardens), has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the LPA. The landscape and ecological management plan shall be carried out as approved, and any subsequent variations shall be agreed in writing by the LPA.
The scheme shall include the following elements:
�	details of the long-term management and maintenance of landscaped and ecological areas
�	details of vegetation management and maintenance regimes
�	details of any new habitat created on-site
�	details of management responsibilities
�	monitoring and review arrangements, where applicable
Reason: To ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat. Also, to secure opportunities for enhancing the site's nature conservation value in line with national planning policy and adopted policy GB5 of the Hounslow Local Plan.
Condition : 88 - River Brent Buffers Details
No development (except demolition, site clearance, ground investigation, and remediation works), associated with the outline element, shall take place until a scheme for the provision and management of an 8-metre-wide buffer zone, measured from the sheet piled river wall forming the River Brent channel, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the LPA. Thereafter, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved scheme. Any subsequent variations shall be agreed in writing by the LPA. Due to the heavily modified condition of the riverbank, the buffer zone scheme is permitted to include built development, including lighting, domestic gardens, footpaths and formal landscaping.
The scheme should be free from non-native plant species and any built development in the buffer zone should be sensitive to wildlife and reflect native riparian character.
The scheme shall include:
�	plans showing the extent and layout of the buffer zone (provided in meter)
�	details of any proposed planting scheme (for example, native species of local provenance)
�	details of measures to protect the buffer zone during construction and implementation of the development
�	details of any proposed footpaths, fencing, lighting, and other infrastructure within the buffer zone

Details of the long-term management and maintenance of the buffer zone shall be secured through the approved Landscape and Ecological Management Plan.
Reason(s): Land alongside watercourses is particularly valuable for wildlife, and it is essential that this is protected. Networks of undeveloped buffer zones might also help wildlife adapt to climate change and will help restore watercourses to a more natural state as required by the Thames River Basin Management Plan.
Condition : 89 - Mobility Hub
Prior to the first occupation of the relevant Phase, full details of the Mobility Hub shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include: 
(a) layout and specification of shared mobility services (including car-club bays, cycle parking, cycle-hire, e-cargo and micro-mobility parking), 
(b) EV-charging infrastructure, 
(c) management and booking arrangements, 
(d)signage and wayfinding, and 
(e) hours of operation, safety measures and maintenance responsibilities. 
The Mobility Hub shall be fully implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the relevant phase and shall thereafter be retained and operated for the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives
Condition : 90 - Fast Food
To support healthy eating and reduce exposure to unhealthy food environments, no additional fast-food and hot-food takeaway premises will be permitted within 400 metres of any school. Applications within this zone will only be considered where it can be clearly demonstrated that they do not contribute to clustering and do not adversely affect opportunities for accessing affordable, healthy food.
Reason: To promote a healthier environment around Schools by limiting takeaway clustering.
Condition : 91 - Flexible Commercial and Community Uses (Detailed Element)
The flexible commercial and community uses falling within Blocks B1, F, G, H, K and L of the development as shown on plan GWR-DHMS-ZZ-00-DR-A-P0100, shall not exceed 2,212sqm GIA of Use Classes E, F and Sui Generis (bar and drinking establishment, car/bike showroom, theatre launderette, dance hall, cinema, hot food takeaway, virtual reality/immersive experience venue and escape room) and shall comprise:
a)	a minimum of 1,877 sqm of total floorspace (GIA) for community Class E(e), E(f), and F uses; and
b)	a maximum of:
10%  of total floorspace (GIA) for car/bike showroom;
10% of total floorspace (GIA for hot food takeaway;
50% of total floorspace (GIA) for bar and drinking establishment;
20% of total floorspace (GIA) for theatre and/or dance hall and/or cinema;
10% of total floorspace (GIA) for virtual reality/immersive experience venue and/or escape room.

Reason: To ensure an appropriately balanced and complementary range of uses on site, and to ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the approved plans and other submitted details and to ensure that the quantum of floorspace keeps within the parameters assessed pursuant to the EIA in relation to the development.
Condition : 92 - Brewery Premises
The brewery premises, excluding potential B2 uses in the J plots,  shall be used solely as a Sui Generis micro-brewery for which there shall be:
(i)	no activity within or from the premises which is of detriment to the amenity of adjoining residents, in relation to noise, vibration, smell or fumes;
(ii)	no B2-type brewing, manufacturing, processing, bottling, canning or distribution activities shall take place on site; and
(iii)	no permitted development rights shall allow any change to a B2 use.
Any change in use shall require full planning permission.
Reason: To protect the appearance of the area and the neighbours' living conditions.
Condition : 93 - M4 Impact
Any part of the development hereby permitted, that sits within the footprint of the elevated M4 motorway, shall not be used for the storage of highly reactive, explosive or flammable substances listed in Parts B and C of Schedule 1 of the Planning (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 1992 (as amended).
Reason: To ensure the operation of the development does not materially affect the safety, reliability and/or operation of the SRN (the tests set out in DfT C2/13 para's 9 & 10 and MHCLG NPPF para 109).
Condition : 94 - Geotechnical and structural assessment impacts upon the M4
No development, in each Phase, shall take place (except for demolition, site clearance, site investigations, remediation, or other facilitating works), shall commence until a detailed Geotechnical and Structural Impact Assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with National Highways (formerly Highways England).
Reason: To ensure the operation of the development does not materially affect safety.
Condition : 95 - Glint and glare and assessment
Any relevant Reserved Matters application involving external fa�ade design should be accompanied by a detailed Solar Glare Assessment. The assessment shall quantify potential glint and glare effects on nearby highways, rail infrastructure, and surrounding buildings, and shall include any necessary mitigation measures (such as fa�ade design amendments, materials specification or shading devices). The approved mitigation shall be fully implemented prior to occupation and thereafter retained.
Reason: To ensure the development does not result in hazardous solar glare impacts on road users, rail users or neighbouring properties, in accordance with local and London-wide safety and amenity policies.
